evidence: Searched all comments in cache/ttl.py (lines 3, 7-11, 13-14, 18, 21-23, 34, 37-39). Every one is in Portuguese, e.g. line 18 'chave -> (valor, instante em que foi gravada)'. Only code names such as get(), put(), MAX_ENTRIES and time.monotonic appear untranslated.

Searched each comment against the line it precedes. Line 18 'chave -> (valor, instante em que foi gravada)' gives the dict's format rather than restating `self._entries = {}`. Line 3 describes eviction behaviour located elsewhere. No comment paraphrases a single statement.
cache/ttl.py:7 '# Cache em memória em que cada entrada expira `ttl_s` segundos depois de gravada.'

Expired entries still count toward MAX_ENTRIES: cache/ttl.py:9-10 'Até lá ela continua ocupando uma das MAX_ENTRIES vagas.' Eviction scans every entry: cache/ttl.py:38-39 'É uma busca linear, O(n) por put() com o cache cheio.'

Checked each claim against the code. Lazy expiry is true (lines 29-30 delete only on get, plus eviction at 40-41). Equal age is still valid because the comparison is `>`. Reading does not renew the TTL. Re-putting a key resets the timestamp and skips eviction because of the `key not in` guard. Eviction picks the minimum stored_at, so it may hit expired or unexpired entries. time.monotonic is unaffected by system clock adjustments. Line 3 'ao atingi-lo, put() descarta a entrada mais antiga' is a loose summary, but line 34 and lines 37-39 qualify it accurately. No false behaviour found.

Searched for any rationale ('porque', 'para', 'motivo', 'escolhido'). The MAX_ENTRIES comment (line 3) only says what the limit does. The clock comment (lines 13-14) states a property of time.monotonic without claiming it was chosen for that reason. No reason is given for 1024 or for any other design choice.
